title: Explain What a Comparison Can Show

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料；尚待独立教学与发音审核。

instructions: Prepare briefly and record your own response of 120–160 words. The sample is shorter than the 90–120 second target. Add relevant details and allow natural pauses while staying within 120–160 words.
prompt: Speak for about 90–120 seconds, using 120–160 words. Describe a fictional comparison of two lights or appliances, state the assumed use and explain one limit of the result. Use at least six lesson words.
reference: I would compare two lights in a community study room. In my fictional example, the first light has a power label of eight watts and the second has a label of twelve watts. If we use each one for five hours, the first gives forty watt-hours and the second gives sixty. Their calculated consumption is unequal, so the first uses less electricity under this assumption. However, the result does not automatically prove that it is more efficient for the task. We would need to compare the amount of useful light and the real usage. An inexpensive price is not the same as a complete annual expense. I would also ask whether daylight is enough during the morning. We cannot make a carbon emission estimate without knowing the electricity source, so I would write that limit beside the chart.
